title: Evaluate an AI assistant that schedules patient follow-ups.
objective: Decide whether to launch a paid pilot.

sections.title: Launch Strategy
sections.body:
## Go with conditions
Launch a paid pilot with **five** clinics (assumption).

executive.recommendation: Launch a **paid pilot with 5 clinics at $149 a month** within the $15k budget, and commit to a wider launch only if 3 of 5 convert to paid by month 4.
executive.overview: An assistant that drafts patient follow-up appointments from clinical notes and books them into the clinic's calendar. The objective is to prove that small clinics pay for fewer missed follow-ups within six months.
executive.opportunity: Small outpatient clinics lose **10-20% of follow-ups** to manual scheduling; EHR add-ons are priced for large groups and reminder tools do not read notes.
executive.strategic_alignment: Fits a solo founder's **six-month runway**: a narrow product sold to a niche the founder can reach directly, with no hardware and managed services only.
executive.financial_case: The plan earns back its **$12k** within two years and has a positive NPV at a 30% discount rate; the pilot gate limits the loss to the pilot budget if clinics do not convert.

market.personas:
**Practice manager Maria** runs a 3-doctor clinic; values calm days and full calendars; loses an hour a day chasing follow-ups.

**Dr. Okafor, owner-physician**, wants fewer no-shows without new software to learn.
market.value_proposition: For small clinics, follow-ups booked from the note in seconds, so fewer patients fall through the cracks, at a tenth of an EHR add-on's price.

channels.approach: Posts and a webinar a month

market.pricing_strategy: **$149 per clinic per month**, flat; pilot at $49 for the first two months.

technical.infrastructure: A web app and API on **Azure App Service**, a Postgres database and a queue for drafting jobs.
technical.stack: Python and FastAPI, Postgres, Azure OpenAI for drafting, Google and Outlook calendar APIs.
technical.scalability: Year one: 50 clinics, ~2,000 notes a day; the drafting workers scale out on queue length.

risk.data_protection: Notes are PHI: **AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit**, role-based access with MFA.
risk.compliance: **HIPAA applies**: BAAs with Azure and every vendor before any real patient data.

risks.mitigation: No real data until BAAs are signed
Staff approve every draft in the pilot

risks.description: Clinics will not pay after the pilot
risks.mitigation: Pilot priced, with a conversion gate at month 4
Spending capped at $15k; stop at month 4 without 3 paying

risks.description: Solo founder is a single point of failure
risks.mitigation: Contractor documents and can run the system

financial.assumptions:
- Year 1: 12 clinics by year end, averaging 6.7 paying × $149 × 12 ≈ **$12k**.
- Churn 3% a month.
